conviction_note: The bar is the bank's own published consensus from 20 brokers, dated 29.10.2026: Q3 net profit PLN 2,815m, range 2,741-2,870. The one line pre-released (CHF legal cost, PLN 371m, report 37/2026) is already in that consensus, from a minimum of 370 to a maximum of 371. The rest are small offsetting read-throughs. The peers that reported 27-30 Oct beat or matched on NII but surprised on corporate provisions; P2G is zero; management's 'strongest year' ambition sits above the mean FY consensus. So p_up is 52 on a 3.5% move, giving +0.14. The findings sum to +0.20 and the two numbers agree in sign. The 3.5% sits above this name's observed results-day median of about 1.8% (five prints 2025-26) because the numbers are new and a peer, mBank, moved 8.6% on its Q3 day. It sits far below the European 7% base because this is a 20-broker mega-cap with a tight bar.

findings.finding: Peers that reported Q3 on 27-30 Oct surprised on corporate provisions. mBank came in 30% above the PAP bar on one construction exposure (CoR 67bp vs 37bp in Q2); Pekao was 7% above on two corporate clients (CoR 61bp). PKO's consensus has credit impairments FALLING 3.7% q/q to 399m, so a provision miss on the largest corporate lender is the main downside risk on the line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measurable for PKO from the sources reached. PKO's CoR has run at 29-30bp through H1 2026, below its strategic level, and no prior provision surprise with a dated reaction was found
findings.original_quote: Saldo rezerw wyniosło 261 mln zł i było o 30 proc. wyższe od konsensusu (...) na wzrost kosztu ryzyka w segmencie bankowości korporacyjnej miało wpływ przede wszystkim zawiązanie rezerwy na jedną większą ekspozycję korporacyjną z branży budowlanej (Provisions of PLN 261m were 30% above consensus (...) the rise in corporate cost of risk was mainly due to a provision on one larger corporate exposure in construction)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly. The PKO consensus is dated 29.10, after mBank (28.10) and Pekao (29.10, 06:49), yet it still has impairments down q/q at 399m, with a max of 454. If brokers had read the peer spikes across, the impairment consensus would be flat to up q/q. It is a proxy: no document says PKO shares the exposure, and ING's provisions came in 45% BELOW its bar, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: Peer NII in Q3 came in line or ahead of the PAP bars: mBank +3.6% (NIM up to 3.6% from 3.5%), ING +1.8%, Pekao and Erste in line, with NIM stabilising q/q at Pekao and Erste. PKO's consensus NII of 6,357 (+4.9% q/q reported) is only about +1.7% over Q2's underlying 6,248 once the -173m Q2 CJEU adjustment is added back, so the bar on PKO's main line looks undemanding.

Its translation into a payout statement is not: the stock fell -1.94% on the next session (02.11), so the fact earned no visible premium, and only the release or call can turn it into a number. Erste Bank Polska got the same letter, so it is not unique to PKO.

findings.finding: In H1 the CEO stated an ambition of 'the strongest year in PKO's history', which means FY2026 net profit above 2025's PLN 10.68bn. The company-compiled FY2026 mean consensus is 10,556 (below that) and the median is 10,972 (above), and it includes forecasts from before the statement. A reiteration on 5 Nov would pull the stragglers up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ambition was stated with the Q2 print on 13.08.2026 (-0.36% that day, then +1.52% the next session)
findings.original_quote: Pierwsze półrocze daje nam mocne podstawy, aby mieć ambicję na najsilniejszy rok w historii PKO Banku Polskiego (The first half gives us a solid basis for the ambition of the strongest year in PKO Bank Polski's history)
findings.why_not_priced: The statement is public, but the FY consensus mean still sits below it (10,556 vs 10,682) because it pools recommendations from 1.04-1.10.2026. If the market fully believed the ambition, the mean would be above 10,682. The finding is small because the median already is, and because 'ambition' is not a guide.

lessons_applied: 'Size the move on what is new; history moves p_up, not abs_move' raised abs_move_pct from 3.0 to 3.5: the numbers other than CHF are new, a peer moved 8.6% on its Q3 day, and the name's own ~1.8% results-day median is no longer used as a cap
'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series' cut the peer-provision read-through from -0.3 to -0.2, because ING's provisions ran 45% below its bar
The peer NII read-through went from +0.2 to +0.1 as partly priced: the consensus was compiled after the peers reported
'A pre-released number is worth 0' confirmed the CHF finding at 0.0; no change
